chapter: Leading his own band in Los Angeles
title: Meeting Louis Armstrong and learning the half-valve glissando
summary: He went backstage at the Cotton Club and Armstrong showed him how to half-valve and tighten the lips to make the slide effect.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well when you say you met Louis for the first time, what happened? Do you remember?

Yes. Well you know Louis played every night. They had this radio program which came from the Cotton Club. And I used to hear him every night aside from his records. By this time I had all of his records. And then at night I'd hear him on the radio. And at that time I didn't know how he could make a trumpet 'gliss' as we say in music. You know, just slide like a trombone. So I couldn't understand how Louis could make a trumpet do that.

So, I say he's got to be playing a slide trumpet to make it come out like that. And the guys in the band said no, he's not playing a slide trumpet, it's the same just like your, the same trumpet. So I said, no, I've got to see it, you know. And Matt had told me down in New Orleans they did that but didn't tell anybody how they did it. They put a handkerchief over their face so nobody could see them do it.

So I didn't know whether Louis would tell me how he did it anyway. But anyway, the Berry Brothers were working out at the Cotton Club. So I arranged to go out to the Cotton Club with Nyus Berry. And I went out early and went back stage and everybody's putting on their costumes and they took me in Louis' room.

And Louis was very nice. He signed his picture for me. And I said, Mr. Armstrong, I said, will you show me how you do this on the trumpet? Well at first he showed me his horn. It was just like mine. So he said, yes, he'd show me. And he did. He showed me, but I had to wait around. He had to go to the bathroom. When he came back from the
bathroom he showed me how to do that. And I learned it that way.
So what was it that you didn't know before? What did he do?

Well he took all three fingers on the valves and pushed the valves half way down so they were half cocked. Then he did the rest with his lips. He just tightened his lips up and that makes the sound go up like a whistle.
You see, by it being half cocked, it doesn't make a note, it makes a sound.
So did you find you could do it after a time?
